title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is the opening of Part II, 'Structure of the 2-torsion in P^1'. It belongs to a manuscript on moduli of elliptic curves in characteristic ≠ 2.

Setting. V is a group isomorphic to (Z/2)^2 (the Klein four-group, called D_2 here). X → S is a P^1-bundle, and 2 is invertible on S (margin note: 'on est en car. ≠ 2'). The object of study is a fibrewise faithful action of V on X, i.e. a monomorphism of group schemes V_S → Aut_S(X) = G, a PGL_2-form.

Step 1: involutions as axes. Fix a basis e_1, e_2 of V. A homomorphism V → Aut_S(X) that is injective on each line F_2 e_i gives two involutions σ_1, σ_2. In characteristic ≠ 2, an involution of a P^1-bundle is the same as its fixed locus Δ_i = X^{σ_i}. This is an étale divisor of degree 2 over S, which Grothendieck calls an 'axis' (the axis of a rotation of order 2).

Step 2: commutation and injectivity. σ_1 and σ_2 commute iff Δ_2 is σ_1-stable, equivalently iff Δ_1 is σ_2-stable. The reason is that σ_1σ_2σ_1 is the involution whose axis is σ_1(Δ_2). The map V_S → G is a monomorphism iff σ_1 ≠ σ_2 fibrewise. For commuting involutions this is equivalent to Δ_1 ∩ Δ_2 = ∅, since two commuting involutions have axes that are either equal or disjoint.

Step 3: parametrising the second involution. Fix σ_1, i.e. Δ_1. Then σ_1 acts freely on X \ Δ_1, and the quotient (X \ Δ_1)/σ_1 is a G_m-torsor-like curve. Giving σ_2, i.e. Δ_2, amounts to giving a section of this quotient over S. Δ_2 is recovered as the preimage of the section, which is an étale double cover, hence an étale divisor of degree 2.

Step 4: the third axis. The third nonzero element e_3 = e_1 + e_2 gives σ_3 = σ_1σ_2 and its axis Δ_3. The three axes are mutually disjoint, so their union is the 'octahedral configuration' of six points. In the standard model these are {0,∞}, {1,-1}, {i,-i}: the vertices of an octahedron, with the three axes joining opposite vertices.

What comes next (from the following page). Étale-locally the situation is unique: Δ_1 = {0,∞}, Δ_2 = {±1}, σ_1(z) = -z, σ_2(z) = 1/z. The purpose is to describe level-2 structures (2-torsion) of elliptic curves through the induced Klein four-action on the quotient E/[-1] ≅ P^1. The normaliser of V in PGL_2 is the octahedral group S_4, which brings in GL_2(F_2) ≅ S_3.
errors: No mathematical errors. The equivalences used (involution ↔ fixed étale degree-2 divisor; commuting ↔ stability of axes; injectivity ↔ disjointness) are correct, given that 2 is invertible, as the margin note records. The text tacitly uses that two commuting involutions have axes that are either equal or disjoint, so disjointness is exactly σ_1 ≠ σ_2; this is correct but left implicit.

ideas.what: Involutions of a P^1-bundle (2 invertible) correspond bijectively to étale degree-2 divisors, their fixed loci or 'axes'.
ideas.modern_name: Fixed-point description of involutions in PGL_2 / twisted forms of μ_2-actions on conics

ideas.what: Klein four-subgroups of PGL_2 over a base: commutation is σ_1-stability of Δ_2, injectivity is disjointness, and the second axis is a section of (X \ Δ_1)/σ_1.
ideas.modern_name: Klein four-group actions on P^1 over a base; moduli of V-actions as a torsor/gerbe
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Klein, Vorlesungen über das Ikosaeder); relative version folklore

ideas.what: The three axes of V form the octahedral configuration of 6 points; this is the start of the link to level-2 structures on elliptic curves via E/[-1] ≅ P^1.
ideas.modern_name: Octahedral configuration; normaliser of V_4 in PGL_2 is S_4; Legendre / level-2 structure
ideas.usually_credited_to: Klein (geometry); level-2 moduli classical (Legendre, Igusa, Deligne–Rapoport)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful, routine relative rewriting of the classical theory of Klein four-subgroups of PGL_2 and the octahedral configuration, set up as preparation for level-2 structures. Nothing here goes beyond what specialists know.
transcription_corrections: Margin note: read 'on est en car. ≠ 2' (characteristic different from 2), not 'on est un ens. ≠ 2'.
Last lines: likely 'Considérons le troisième élément ≠ 0, e_3 = e_1 + e_2, il lui correspond un axe Δ_3, et Δ_1, Δ_2, Δ_3 sont mutuellement disjoints.'
Phrase near (1): read 'la donnée d'un homom.' — the '[?]' can be dropped.
The inserted phrase reads roughly 'i.e. d'une involution de X, ou encore, de celle d'un axe (diviseur étale de degré 2)', applied to each of e_1, e_2.
